::: {.meta}
Data source, year, and unit of analysis. One line.
:::

The question you started with, and what the data actually said. Two or three
short paragraphs. Lead with the finding.

## The finding

State it in plain language with real numbers. A reader who knows nothing about
the dataset should understand it. No jargon, no code, no acronyms you have not
already spelled out.

## What surprised me

The part that was harder than it looked, or the thing you had to correct. This
is what separates a writeup from a screenshot, and it is usually the paragraph
people remember.

```{=html}
<div class="viz-wrap">
<iframe class="viz viz-short" title="DASHBOARD NAME" loading="lazy"
  src="https://public.tableau.com/views/WORKBOOK-NAME/SHEET-NAME?:showVizHome=no&:embed=true&:toolbar=no&:device=desktop"></iframe>
</div>
```

::: {.viz-note}
[Open full size on Tableau Public](PASTE-FULL-TABLEAU-URL)
:::

## How it was built

Describe the analysis in sentences, not code. What the source file contained,
what you had to derive because it was not in there, and how you checked that the
derivation was right. If there is a script, put it in the code folder and link
it at the bottom rather than pasting it here.

::: {.detail}
Source
: Where the data came from, including year and level of aggregation.

Tools
: What you used and what you actually did with it.

Notes
: Suppression, derived measures, comparability limits, anything a careful reader
  should know before quoting a number.
:::
